title: windowed-arbiter-with-kv-priority-expiry-and-oscillation-damper
author: Marcus Li
release_notes: Introduces a windowed arbiter and KV-priority expiry to reduce starvation and oscillation in the continuous batcher; rollout guarded by canary and config flags.
description: Motivation: we have seen two related issues in high-concurrency production workloads: (1) intermittent starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests caused by long-lived KV-heavy sequences that pin slots, and (2) oscillatory shifts in the batching frontier when per-tenant burst patterns change rapidly, which increased P99 token latency. This PR introduces a windowed arbiter for the continuous batcher that enforces short, rolling fairness windows and an expiry-based decay for KV priority marks so that heavy requests do not permanently dominate scheduling decisions. Design summary: - Windowed arbiter: requests are admitted into discrete, overlapping micro-windows (configurable window_ms, default 25ms). Within a window, the arbiter computes fair shares using normalized weights, then applies a small randomized jitter to admission deadlines to avoid synchronization-induced oscillation between queues. - KV priority expiry: requests tagged as KV-heavy receive a transient priority boost; that mark now decays after expiry_ms (configurable, default 200ms) instead of being sticky. Expiry is stored as an epoch token in the request descriptor; when the KV cache hits are replenished, the token is refreshed only up to a configurable cap to avoid re-entrancy amplification. - Oscillation damper: a token-based soft-preemption mechanism prevents repeated preemption of the same queue within a short horizon (damper_ms, default 75ms). If a queue gets preempted, its eviction penalty decays linearly, limiting oscillatory thrashing. - Adaptive timeouts with jitter: per-request soft-timeouts are derived from observed tail latencies per route. We attach a small randomized jitter to timeouts to de-correlate client retry patterns when fallbacks trigger. - Kernel hinting: the arbiter exposes a short-lived kernel hint with expected sequence length and kv_hint flag to the compilation/kernel-selection layer so that the runtime can favor tiled attention kernels or different KV cache eviction policies for anticipated long-running sequences. - Backpressure probe: when free slots are low, the arbiter injects low-priority probe admits (hedging) to measure real capacity; probes are rate-limited and labeled for observability. Implementation notes: - New module: runtime/batcher/windowed_arbiter.rs (Rust) handles window state, fairness calculation, and jittered deadlines. - New module: runtime/scheduler/kv_priority.rs implements the expiry token and KV-mark lifecycle. - Minor changes in runtime/alloc/slot_manager.go to add soft-preemption tokens and expose an API for the damper state. - Integrations in runtime/metrics to emit window occupancy, expiration_rate, damper_evictions and probe_success_rate for dashboards. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for fairness math (edge cases with skewed weights), expiry token lifecycle, and damper time-decay were added. - A synthetic load test harness (bench/continuous_bench.py) validates P50/P95/P99 behavior across mixed KV/plain traffic. - Canary in staging: we ran a 48-hour canary across three machines with production-like traffic and observed a 12% P99 reduction for latency-sensitive routes and a 7% improvement in throughput for mixed workloads. Rollout plan: - Feature guarded behind runtime config: enable_windowed_arbiter, kv_priority_expiry_ms, damper_ms. - Canary: staged rollout with 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic gating tied to observed SLOs. - Metrics to watch: p99_latency_routeA, window_occupancy, expiry_reapply_rate, damper_evictions. Backout plan: disable feature flag and revert head if regressions observed for more than two consecutive deployment windows. Migration considerations: - No schema changes to stored models or persistent KV; all state is in-memory and epoch-based. - Default flags remain off for Dedicated regions until QA sign-off. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-2193) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration bench validated - [x] CI passing - [x] Docs: runtime tuning notes updated in docs/perf/batcher.md - [x] Rollout plan documented in PR description Observability updates: dashboards for expiry_reapply_rate and damper_evictions were added; new traces tag window_id included in batcher traces. Related work: this complements prior fair-share and lease-based work (see ENG-1503) and replaces the earlier TTL-based KV-deprioritization experiment which caused abrupt fairness shifts.

review_comments: Ava Chandra: Can you clarify how the expiry token interacts with KV cache refill events? Might user flows with interleaved prefetching reapply priority repeatedly?
Marcus Li: We cap token refresh to once per token_lifetime window (configurable). Refill events can refresh but only up to the cap to prevent amplification; added unit test to validate behavior.
Priya Nair: The damper_ms default seems conservative; can we make it tenant-configurable and add a safety upper-bound?
Marcus Li: Damper is tenant-configurable in the new config map with an upper-bound (500ms). Documented in runtime tuning notes.
Diego Ramos: CI flake on test_kv_priority on first run; looks like a timing assumption in test harness. Please make assertions tolerant to jitter.
Marcus Li: Adjusted tests to use eventual assertions with 200ms slack; CI re-ran and passed.
ci_summary: Initial CI hit a timing flake on test_kv_priority (fixed by using eventual assertions). Full suite now passes on Linux amd64 and macos-latest. Bench harness run completed in staging with expected improvements.
notes: This change is intentionally conservative: defaults are feature-flagged and off for Dedicated until product QA signs off. Operators can tune window_ms, kv_priority_expiry_ms and damper_ms per deployment.
